Meta aspires to a global launch. “[We] are quite excited to bring personal agents to billions of people around the world,” Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, told the Financial Times.
Some startups are already building agents in markets that Big Tech hopes to reach. For instance, South African startup ManyHands offers Manny, a personal assistant designed to order groceries, book appointments and make payments through WhatsApp. But adapting agents to local conditions has its challenges. Anton Moulder, ManyHands’ founder, told Rest of World that getting the AI assistant to converse in all of South Africa’s 11 official spoken languages has been difficult.
Rest of World spoke to AI researchers and other experts to understand how these personal agents would perform outside Western nations.
Would AI agents understand the local language and culture?

articles.summary:
The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
Agility Robotics’ first practical robotic worker is nothing like I dreamed
Agility Robotics, the company I cofounded out of my robotics lab at Oregon State University in 2015, has just launched Digit 5. It’s designed to be the first humanoid robot that can safely and economically do useful work at scale, allowing us to bring tens of thousands of humanoid workers into the real world. Engineered to lift 23-kilogram bins onto high shelves and with a battery that can run for 90 minutes on a 9-minute charge, Digit 5’s goal is to handle heavy warehouse tasks shift after shift, filling the need for labor in jobs that are too physically stressful or too dull for humans to want to do.
Digit 5 is what Agility has been working toward for over a decade. But the robot is heavy and bulky, lacking the graceful natural motion of its predecessors, and it’s farther than I thought possible from the robot I dreamed of building when I started this company. To deliver a useful commercial product, Agility has taken a path that is very different from what I first imagined.

My dream has always been to build robots that combine locomotion and manipulation to move through the world and interact with it as people do. I seek a mastery of motion, achieved through devices designed to navigate the constraints of physics with elegance. The recent disclosure of a major vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler pointed to a widespread weak point: a login page is an attack surface that can be used to compromise and access an application server. As with any emergency patch, admins had to weigh cutting off or disrupting their users’ access with the risk of delaying a critical security update.
If you’re a NetScaler customer and you haven’t patched your instance, stop reading and go do that. This was a bad one. Once you’ve finished the patch, we’ll explore how to avoid a future fire drill by laying additional security controls.

articles.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) is a Python-based DSL and parallel programming model for NVIDIA GPUs that automatically leverages advanced hardware capabilities to deliver peak performance for tile-level GPU programming. By abstracting thread- and warp-level scheduling behind high-level, tile-centric primitives, cuTile enables you to write GPU kernels in Python while compiler optimizations automatically target advanced hardware features like Tensor Cores.
As an early adopter of cuTile, machine learning engineers at Jane Street implemented Mamba-2, a state-of-the-art sequence model, in cuTile and partnered with NVIDIA to optimize the kernels. Jane Street is a deeply technical global trading firm, using deep learning to drive innovation in advanced quantitative research. This post walks you through the three custom kernels powering the Mamba-2 forward pass and the cuTile optimizations behind them.
Overview and prerequisites
To use cuTile, ensure your environment meets the requirements outlined in the cuTile Python Quickstart guide. Import the package as cuda.tile and expose it as ct throughout the kernel implementations featured in this post.

articles.title: Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM
Multi-turn agentic workloads build on accumulated context as an agent reasons, invokes tools, and incorporates earlier results. With each new turn, the client resends the conversation history, including system instructions, prior prompts, tool results, and model responses, causing the growing context to be processed repeatedly. In Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation, each request is split across specialized nodes: the prefill node processes the prompt and builds its key-value (KV) cache, then the decode node retrieves those KV blocks and generates the response.
Conventional disaggregated serving, however, only transfers KV cache in one direction: from prefill to decode node. This one-directional flow creates two inefficiencies for multi-turn workloads. First, after generating a response, the decode node holds KV cache entries for both the prompt and the newly generated tokens. When processing the next turn, the prefill node cannot retrieve those entries, so it must recompute the KV projections for the previous response tokens. Second, the decode node maintains the session state while the prefill nodes don’t, increasing the probability of cache eviction for active sessions on the prefill nodes. On a full cache miss, the prefill node must recompute KV projections for the entire conversation history, including system instructions, prior user requests, tool results, and m…

Ever tried to shrink your container images to reduce their attack surface? If you have, you’ve likely discovered a frustrating paradox: shrinking a container often blinds your vulnerability scanners to what’s inside.
We’re facing an industry-wide tension between reducing container attack surfaces and maintaining the security visibility you need. To understand how we got here, and how we can solve it, we have to look at how we historically built containers, and why the current approaches fall short for Day 2 operations.
The anatomy of container bloat
For a long time, full container images were the industry standard. The workflow was simple: developers pulled a base image that included a complete operating system, bundled their application code on top, and shipped it to production.

Iida Piano, une petite société japonaise a mis en ligne le 18 octobre le site de reTONE. Le but de cette application est transformer nos vieux smartphones en lecteurs musicaux, de l’écran d’accueil jusqu’à l’écran de verrouillage. Atout de taille, elle accepte des téléphones sous Android 4.0, une version sortie en 2011.
La France a de quoi faire. En 2019, une étude de l’AFNUM, la fédération des industriels du numérique, menée avec l’ADEME, estimait qu’entre 22 et 45 millions de smartphones encore fonctionnels dormaient dans les tiroirs des Français.
Une fois installée, reTONE peut prendre la place de l’écran d’accueil d’Android. Le téléphone s’allume alors directement sur la bibliothèque musicale et l’écran de verrouillage affiche la pochette en plein écran. Un mode « DAP silencieux » (DAP pour digital audio player, le nom anglais des baladeurs audio) coupe notifications, sonneries et alarmes, puis remet les volumes d’origine quand on le désactive.
reTONE ne passera pas par le Play Store. Il faudra télécharger le fichier APK sur le site officiel et l’installer à la main. Pas besoin d’accès root ni de ROM personnalisée, et une désinstallation suffit pour retrouver le téléphone tel qu’il était. Iida Piano promet aussi zéro publicité, aucune collecte de données et des fonctions réseau désactivées par défaut.

articles.title: Permis de conduire valable 15 ans : la France va dire adieu au permis à vie
articles.summary:
Plus que quelques mois. La France, comme une grande partie des États membres de l’Union européenne, n’a plus que quelques mois pour mettre en place la réforme votée le 21 octobre 2025. Celle-ci instaure une nécessité de renouveler son permis de conduire tous les 15 ans. Adoptée à 339 voix pour et 240 voix contre, la directive (UE) 2025/2205 datée du 22 octobre 2025 signe la fin du permis à vie dans les États qui le proposent, France en tête.
Le délai légal pour la mise en place de cette directive est fixé à trois ans après la signature. Concrètement, cela revient à dire que la mesure doit être appliquée en France avant le 21 octobre 2028. Il reste moins de deux ans au gouvernement pour engager ce changement. La France n’est d’ailleurs pas la seule à prendre son temps : ils ne seraient que cinq États, sur les vingt-deux à avoir officiellement franchi le pas (Italie, Danemark, Pays-Bas, Finlande et Portugal).
Que prévoit le texte ?
Le texte européen voté l’an dernier prévoit qu’un contrôle médical doit être effectué tous les quinze ans afin de renouveler la validité du permis de conduire pour une nouvelle période de quinze ans. C’est un cadre légal minimum, c’est-à-dire que chaque État membre est libre de durcir les règles.
Le seul durcissement évoqué par la directive européenne concerne les conducteurs de plus de 65 ans. Le Parlement européen précise que les pays de l’UE peuvent réduire la durée de validité du permis pour les conducteurs âgés de 65 ans ou plus, afin de les sou…

articles.summary:
Des vitrines brisées, des boutiques saccagées et des individus qui repartent les bras chargés de marchandises. Les scènes de pillage se sont multipliées le samedi 17 octobre 2026 en France, en marge des manifestations contre la vie chère et les conditions d’études. Les commerces de téléphonie et d’électronique n’ont pas été épargnés parmi les 1 500 commerces touchés, avec plusieurs boutiques saccagées de SFR à Paris, Orange à Rennes, la Fnac à Nantes ou encore l’Apple Store de Lille et de Bordeaux.

Un vêtement dérobé peut facilement changer de mains sans que son propriétaire puisse le retrouver. Pour un smartphone, c’est une autre histoire : plusieurs dispositifs permettent de bloquer son utilisation, en coupant son accès aux réseaux mobiles ou en verrouillant directement l’appareil.

articles.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
articles.summary:
Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
Today, we're announcing a preview of a new class of System One-style models: extraction models. Our first one, Clairic, is available hosted on Workers AI as @cf/cloudflare/clairic.We intend to release the model open-weights soon. Clairic is an extraction model that is able to extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs — all at a significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and cheaper cost than traditional LLMs.
Context
When System One models were announced by TypeSafe a month ago, it took the industry by storm. As referenced by TypeSafe in their blog and defined by Daniel Kahneman’s book Thinking, Fast and Slow, a System One model should be fast and precise, which contrasts a System Two model that is capable of deliberate reasoning (like LLMs). With this, TypeSafe introduced Jev — a model that is purpose-fit for a specific use case, and priced accessibly given its niche domain. It excelled where LLMs failed, helping users make decisions based on probabilities and well-typed outputs. The introduction of Jev prompted people to start thinking about a new class of models that were not LLMs and how to integrate them into their workflows.
We were inspired by the concept of System One models and started thinking about other tasks where LLMs are inefficient. There are many structured-output calls going to frontier LLMs today with the same shapes again and again: What's the invoice total?…

Outras áreas mais tradicionais, como ciência de dados, engenharia de software e segurança da informação, já batem os R$ 40 mil. Va-t-on enfin savoir comment Mars a obtenu ses minuscules lunes ? Idéfix, le rover français décollera le 19 octobre à bord de MMX, la mission japonaise. Le petit véhicule va devoir apprivoiser une gravité totalement folle pour aider à collecter des échantillons et les ramener sur Terre.
C'est l'un des décollages les plus attendus de l'année pour une mission extrêmement ambitieuse. Et la France y prend part très activement. Le 19 octobre prochain, la mission internationale MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) doit s'envoler avec comme objectif de percer enfin les mystères des deux lunes de Mars, Phobos et Deimos.
Portée par la JAXA (Japon) aux côtés du CNES, du DLR, de la NASA et de l'ESA, la mission embarque une armada d'instruments de précision et un petit rover éclaireur prénommé Idefix. Décryptage d'un défi d'ingénierie hors norme.
D'où viennent les deux petites lunes martiennes ?
En ligne de mire scientifique : trancher un débat vieux de plusieurs décennies. Phobos et Deimos sont-elles de simples astéroïdes capturés par la gravité martienne ou sont-elles nées des débris projetés lors d'un choc titanesque subi par Mars dans sa jeunesse ?
La mission MMX décollera à bord du nouveau lanceur lourd japonais H3, récemment certifié après des débuts chaotiques et quelques explosions. Les récents tirs ont été des succès rassurants (voir en fin d'article).

articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Microsoft has fixed a known issue that removed the Copilot Chat and Copilot buttons in the classic Outlook desktop mail client for some Windows users.

- The Copilot button missing from the top-right area above the ribbon.
- The Copilot icon missing from the left app bar or More Apps area in classic Outlook.
- In Add Apps, Copilot may appear as an available app, but selecting Open does nothing.
- Adding Copilot through ribbon customization may show the command as unavailable or grayed out.

Microsoft first announced in June that it had fixed the bug with a service change, but last month it said it had started investigating again after recent updates caused it to resurface.
Now, Microsoft says it has finally resolved this classic Outlook issue, blaming it on a bug that prevented Outlook from retrieving some account information from the user's Outlook profile.

articles.title: Anthropic Acquires Confidential AI Startup Opaque Systems
articles.summary:
Anthropic has acquired Opaque Systems, a company that developed technology for using sensitive data in AI systems while keeping it protected by the underlying hardware.
Opaque announced the deal last week, saying its team is joining Anthropic. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Opaque started as a research project at UC Berkeley’s RISELab a decade ago. Its founders include Ion Stoica, co-founder of Databricks and Anyscale, and Raluca Ada Popa, an encryption and systems security researcher who now works at Google DeepMind. Aaron Fulkerson joined as CEO in October 2023.
The company turned its confidential computing research into technology used in production AI deployments. Over time, it broadened that work beyond protecting data and models.
“As AI evolved, so did the problem we set out to solve. Protecting data and models was no longer enough. Organizations also needed a way to independently verify how AI systems and agents behaved,” Opaque said.
“That led us to expand our work from confidential AI to verifiable AI: replacing trust assumptions with cryptographic evidence of what ran, where it ran, and under what policies,” the company added.
Opaque also worked with the wider community on open projects that address trust and security for AI agents and models. These include the Agent Governance Toolkit, TRACE, Confidential MCP and Weight Custody Manifest.
Opaque this year raised a $24 million Series B round at a $300 million valuation. The company listed Anthropic among its cus…

articles.title: DeepSeek made its name with cheap AI models. Now it’s undercutting search API rivals, too.

DeepSeek made its name with cheap AI models. Now it’s undercutting search API rivals, too.
Not content with challenging the major frontier AI labs with lower-cost models, Chinese AI company DeepSeek is setting its sights on the search API market.
On Saturday, the company announced it has opened up its internally developed search engine to outside developers through two new APIs, Search and Fetch, allowing them to retrieve live web search results and webpage content for use in their own apps and agents.
Both services cost $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests, and developers can use them independently of DeepSeek’s AI models.
The launch also came alongside DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a minor update to the V4.1 Flash model the company released in September.
Why AI agents need web search
Large language models (LLMs) are trained on data collected up to a certain point in time, meaning they can’t always answer questions about recent events, updated documentation, or any other kind of dynamic information. By supporting live web search, models can retrieve current information from the internet, which supplements their responses.
For developers building AI agents, this is particularly important. A coding agent, for example, might need to consult the latest software documentation, investigate a recently disclosed vulnerability, or otherwise check that a particular library has been updated.

articles.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable.
“Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence, told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.”
Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it.
“Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said.
Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15. It will present on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday afternoon, October 13.
Sun, alongside his co-founder and chief scientist Henry Liu, founded Laplace a year ago out of the University of Michigan. Sun has spent the last eight years in academia researching how to challenge autonomous driving AI in simulation. In 2023, he and Liu — his then-PhD adviser — published a paper on the subject that made it onto the cover of the top scientific journal Nature. That’s when the calls started coming in from auto…

Lauren Hauswirth, ResolvMD

articles.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
articles.summary:
Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
When we previously blogged about our AI code reviewer in April, an average review cost a palatable $1.19. By the end of August, that figure had shot up to about $2.46. We hadn't made any significant architectural changes: the coordinator was still handing work to the same set of specialist reviewers, and the same risk tiers decided how intensive of a review we gave.
Around mid-September we tasked our agents with working out where those tokens were going and cutting them — aggressively. With code quality at high effort, the average review now costs just $0.77, down 68% from the $2.43 it averaged over our two most expensive weeks before we started. Our main goal was to cut costs, but as part of this work we also managed to optimize the reviewer, so that the median review now takes just 1m 32s instead of the 4m 09s it took before.
About 40% of the savings came from changes and optimizations to the reviewer's code, and the rest from experimenting with which models we use and how much effort they put in.

articles.title: Los despidos sin indemnizar ni justificar se disparan tras la reforma laboral y ya suman casi 3,2 millones
articles.summary:
Los contratos indefinidos también pueden durar semanas; durante el periodo de prueba la empresa puede, con carácter general, acabar con la relación laboral sin tener que indemnizar y sin acreditar una causa. Su uso ha ido en aumento desde la reforma laboral de 2022; las bajas que se acumulan están en torno a los 3,2 millones, según Colpisa.
La información puede recogerse en la tabla de la Seguridad Social: en el periodo comprendido entre enero de 2022 y agosto de 2026 se registran 3.188.254 bajas por no superar la prueba con contratos indefinidos; los datos de 2026 son provisionales.
Hay que tener en cuenta lo antecedente: en 2025 se registraron 723.763, frente a los 75.004 de 2021, lo que son casi diez veces más. Si lo comparamos con 2019 (justo antes de la pandemia), las cifras fueron de 132.534, y el último año completo multiplica esa cifra por 5,46.
Nosotros ya hablamos del repunte de estos ceses. La dificultad que esto plantea se encuentra en que un contrato indefinido no tiene fecha de finalización; sin embargo, es algo que no impide que pueda terminar durante la prueba. Para quien ha cambiado de trabajo, tal posibilidad puede afectar a la estabilidad prevista por el contrato y a la protección por desempleo.
Una empresa puede prescindir de un trabajador porque no se ha adaptado al puesto, pero también (y aquí entra la picaresca) puede utilizar la prueba para una necesidad temporal. Las estadísticas que conocemos no permiten calcular cuántas de estas bajas son fraudulent…

articles.title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM
vLLM is an open-source inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). LLM inference has two distinct phases: prefill, which processes the input prompt and builds the key-value (KV) cache, and decode, which uses that cache to generate output one token at a time. These phases have different compute, memory, and scaling characteristics. Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation runs them on separate engine instances, allowing each phase to scale and be optimized independently. This can improve resource utilization, throughput, and latency under load. However, it also requires transferring the KV cache from the prefill instance to the decode instance before token generation can begin, making efficient KV transfer critical to time-to-first-token (TTFT).
One of the ways vLLM performs this transfer is through the NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library (NIXL) connector, which moves KV blocks over interconnects that support Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA), such as AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (AWS EFA, the low-latency RDMA network used across servers in AWS). On supported instance types, AWS EFA supports GPUDirect RDMA and Neuron Direct RDMA. NIXL can therefore transfer KV blocks directly between GPU or AWS Trainium device memory without staging through host memory. Amazon has signed an agreement with X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP) to fund the building of a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana. The proposed plant, which would replace the now defunct coal-fueled Breed Generating Station in Fairbanks, Sullivan County, aims to provide up to 960 megawatts of carbon-free energy for both the regional power grid and Amazon’s data centers.
Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
The proposed nuclear plant would provide 960 megawatts to power the grid — and Amazon’s data centers.
No timeline for construction or operation has been announced for the facility, which Amazon says “could” create 1,000 construction jobs and 100 permanent roles. The facility in Indiana is targeting to build 12 Xe-100 SMR’s, an advanced (but unproven) reactor that’s still undergoing development and licensing. These reactors can be cooled using either air, water, or a hybrid solution of both, which Amazon says should allow them to be deployed in water-constrained regions without impacting water demand in local communities.
Indiana also happens to be home to a famously expensive and uncompleted energy project called the Marble Hill Nuclear Power Plant. It was abandoned half-finished in 1983 after $2.5 billion had already been sunk into it, and has been under continued demolition since 2008. O vírus Coxsackie, conhecido por causar a síndrome mão-pé-boca, geralmente provoca infecções leves, mas, em casos raros, pode atingir o coração e provocar alterações no ritmo cardíaco. Foi o que aconteceu com o apresentador Carlos Alberto de Nóbrega, de 90 anos, que precisou de um marcapasso após uma infecção agravar uma insuficiência cardíaca preexistente.
Internado no Hospital Sírio-Libanês, em São Paulo (SP), desde a semana passada, o apresentador contraiu o Coxsackie tipo 2. A infecção agravou seu quadro cardíaco, provocando bradicardia, condição em que o coração bate mais devagar do que o normal, e outras arritmias.
A cirurgia para implantação do aparelho, inicialmente prevista para segunda-feira (19), foi adiada para terça-feira (20). Segundo a assessoria, Carlos Alberto está estável e sem complicações. Sua esposa, Renata de Nóbrega, que é médica, também apresentou sintomas da infecção, mas não precisou ser internada.
O que é o vírus Coxsackie?

Orange pour les plus froides, blanches comme le Soleil, bleu pâle pour les plus chaudes : la couleur d'une étoile se lit d'ordinaire comme un thermomètre. Un outil pirate qui combine 4 failles de sécurité
Les offensives reposent sur l’utilisation d’un outil pirate, Plex2Shell, récemment apparu en ligne. - Date:

- Source:

- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.
How Scientists Tested Perceptions of AI Consciousness

articles.title: One pilot, two aircraft: F-22 Raptor directs autonomous combat drone in glimpse of future air warfare
articles.summary:
What just happened? The US Air Force has announced the military's latest move toward an autonomous future. This time, an F-22 Raptor pilot directed a drone during simulated combat. The pilot issued high-level tactical directives to the YFQ-44A while flying, essentially turning it into an unpiloted wingman.
The demonstration took place earlier this month, when the Raptor and Anduril's YFQ-44A Fury took off from Edwards Air Force Base in California.
Once airborne, the pilot sent an updated mission plan over a tactical data link. The drone's onboard software interpreted those instructions and carried out the maneuvers and simulated combat tasks.
While it might sound like it, this wasn't a case of someone flying two aircraft at once. The pilot decided what the Fury should do, while the autonomous system handled the flight controls.
The test was part of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program. The initiative's aim is to field low-cost, semi-autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles that fly alongside crewed fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets.
The test involved just one Raptor and one Fury, but the longer-term ambition is for a single pilot to direct several autonomous wingmen. Those aircraft could bring extra weapons, sensors, and electronic warfare equipment to a mission.

The organization says the biggest change in ATT&CK v20 is “expanded coverage of recent adversary activity and tradecraft.”
The Enterprise domain gets nine additions, counting both techniques and sub-techniques. Prompt injection is now tracked as two techniques, one for malicious instructions typed straight into an LLM’s interface and one for instructions hidden in material the model ingests.
Another technique describes attackers using an organization’s own AI agents to steal data. Sub-techniques also cover poisoning web content to sway AI search and assistant recommendations, and disrupting LLM-assisted analysis of malware.

articles.title: F5 releases out-of-band patches for critical NGINX vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
F5 has released out-of-band security patches to address multiple NGINX web server flaws, including three critical-severity vulnerabilities that can let attackers execute code on vulnerable systems.
The three critical vulnerabilities were found in the ngx_http_v3_module (CVE-2026-15176 and CVE-2026-97205) and the NGINX map directive (CVE-2026-93479).
Remote attackers without privileges can exploit them to launch denial-of-service (DoS) attacks or gain code execution on NGINX systems with non-default configurations.
Successful exploitation causes a heap-based buffer overflow or use-after-free in the NGINX worker process, leading to crashes or a restart. However, attackers may also be able to "execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR."
F5 released security patches for multiple NGINX software products affected by these two vulnerabilities, including NGINX Plus, NGINX Open Source, NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX Gateway Fabric, and NGINX Instance Manager.
Security teams and admins who can't immediately install these security patches can mitigate CVE-2026-15176 by not using the 'alias' directive in a location block or the $request_filename variable, and CVE-2026-97205 by disabling asynchronous file I/O (AIO) or Server Side Includes (SSI).
CVE-2026-93479 can also be mitigated by using named captures instead of unnamed captures and limiting their use to the block with the regex match.

articles.title: From Macro to Micro, and Back - EE Times
articles.summary:
Looking at this year’s Nobel prizes, I was struck by how many of them explain the behavior of a large system through its smallest parts.
Four different Nobel prizes, one common theme
The medicine prize went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for optogenetics. Hegemann and Nagel found that a protein from green algae could make cells respond to light, and Deisseroth put its gene into neurons, so researchers can switch specific brain cells on and off with a flash of light. For the first time, neuroscientists could test what an individual neuron does and how groups of neurons produce memories, feelings, and behavior.
The chemistry prize went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for their work on chirality, the property of molecules that come in two mirror-image forms, like our left and right hands. Living organisms use only one form of each, and the long-standing puzzle was how that happened. Soai found a reaction in which a minuscule imbalance between the two forms amplifies itself, which the Nobel Committee described as the first time anyone had created chirality from non-chiral molecules since the dawn of life. It is a striking example of micro shaping macro, since a tiny imbalance between individual molecules, amplified by feedback, ended up determining a property of all life on Earth.

articles.title: La psicología dice que las personas que dejan el móvil boca abajo no es para ocultar nada; en realidad, es una táctica para evitar distracciones

Una comida, dos personas. Antes de que llegue la primera ración, uno de los comensales gira su teléfono y lo deja sobre el mantel con la pantalla hacia abajo. Hay quien lo interpreta como desconfianza, pero la explicación es otra: quiere librarse de las notificaciones y las llamadas entrantes y de la presión constante de estar disponible en todo momento. Al fin y al cabo, es solo una interpretación, y no se apoya en ningún experimento científico que estudie sus motivaciones.
Lo que sí han estudiado los experimentos es el efecto de tener el móvil a la vista.
En la Universidad de Essex, Andrew Przybylski y Netta Weinstein realizaron un experimento con parejas de desconocidos que hablaban entre ellos durante diez minutos con un teléfono o un cuaderno sobre una mesa cercana.
En su trabajo, publicado en el Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, el teléfono se asoció con una menor cercanía y una conversación de menor calidad y, en un segundo experimento, con una menor confianza y empatía, aunque solo cuando hablaban de algo personal: con un tema trivial no hubo diferencias. Después, otro grupo de científicos, ya fuera del Reino Unido, llevó la comparación a conversaciones reales.
Shalini Misra, de Virginia Tech, observó 100 conversaciones reales entre dos personas en entornos informales. Aquellas que tuvieron lugar sin ningún dispositivo a la vista salieron mejor valoradas. “En presencia de un dispositivo móvil hay menos contacto visual”, resumía la investigadora.

Las dos empresas marcaban el rumbo de los videojuegos a comienzos de los 90, al menos en el ámbito doméstico. Y cada una necesitaba distinguirse con algún rasgo único. En Sega optaron por la velocidad.
Sonic iba rápido, la Mega Drive no. El hardware de la máquina no estaba mal para la época, pero tenía ciertas limitaciones. El obstáculo estaba, principalmente, en el procesador: el Motorola 68000 que montaba, a 7,67 MHz, era un chip bastante apto, pero carecía de un componente especializado en cálculos matemáticos complejos. Sus 64 KB de memoria RAM tampoco ayudaban (con otros 64 KB dedicados a vídeo).
Dado que Mega Drive necesitaba un Sonic a la altura para vender la máquina, en Sega le encargaron el proyecto a Yuji Naka, cocreador de la saga. Según explicaba en este vídeo con motivo del vigésimo aniversario de Sonic, Yuji tenía claro que los programadores no podían renunciar a la velocidad.
Naka lo explicaba así al recordar el origen del proyecto:
"Me gustan las cosas rápidas y pensé que sería interesante crear un juego en el que, cuanto más hábil te volvieras, menos tiempo necesitaras para completar un nivel".

articles.summary:
In February 2026, the operator of OnlyFake pleaded guilty in the United States for his role in a service that generated more than 10,000 fraudulent digital identity documents. Customers could create passports, driver’s licenses, Social Security cards, and documents from dozens of countries, then choose whether each appeared as a scan or a photograph of a physical ID.
According to the U.S. Department of Justice, the documents allowed cybercriminals to conceal their identities, circumvent identity checks at banks and cryptocurrency exchanges, and launder money.
The activity extends beyond fabricated documents. In underground communities monitored by Flare's platform, actors advertise manipulated photographs and videos, assistance with live identity verification, and accounts they claim have already passed identity checks.
Each year, Flare collects hundreds of thousands of search results related to Know Your Client (KYC) services and the trade in verified accounts. Activity observed between March and September 2026 shows how these offerings are packaged and promoted across underground markets.
What is KYC?
It is the process that financial institutions use to establish a customer’s identity and assess the risk of providing services to them.
Depending on the level of risk, they may validate the document, compare its photograph with a live image, confirm control of contact details, request information about the source of funds, and screen the customer against sanctions and politica…

ETS is a nonprofit that handles state and federally mandated testing under a contract with the state. The organization supports California’s CAASPP and ELPAC assessment programs and relied on a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site to share testing data with CDE.

How far can we push computing?
Nowadays big advances are made by scaling up—think more chips packed into ever-bigger data centers. But as we near the ceiling of what we can build, there’s still plenty of room below, at the fundamental physical limits of computing.
MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can read more from the series here.
On the evening of December 29, 1959, at an American Physical Society meeting at Caltech, the physicist Richard Feynman gave a lecture called “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom,” on how we might manipulate and control things on an extremely small scale. There is no physical law stopping us from writing the entire Encyclopædia Britannica on the head of a pin, he argued, or from storing every book ever written in something the size of a dust speck—or, ultimately, from arranging matter atom by atom. Biology already did versions of this (a living cell keeps its instructions in a wisp of DNA), so all of this was plainly permitted by the laws of physics. We simply had not built the tools yet.
In other words, there was plenty of room at the bottom. He was right, and for decades we descended into that space almost for free. The transistor—the switch at the heart of computer chips—repeatedly halved in size so that chips doubled in density; a computer that once filled a room now fits inside a watch. But that easy descent has now stalled…

Engineer builds tiny 3D-printed single-motor drone in their bedroom — 45-degree hinged rotor and sub-0.2ms firmware control pitch and roll
Single-motor drones could be technically simpler than helicopters or quadcopters, but they require a lot more complex programming.
A software engineer who’s also into drones and 3D printing has shared a single-motor drone that they built inside their home and tested on their bed. Joshua Bird shared a video of how they created it on YouTube, highlighting the unique technique they used to maintain controllability and stability. The design used a combination of a hinged propeller, rapid changes to the motor’s rotation speed, and a custom flight controller and motor controller firmware that allowed the motor to react to necessary changes in under 0.2 milliseconds.
Most rotary wing aircraft require a mechanism to counteract the torque generated by the motor or engine and to change its flight direction, typically with the use of a swash plate to change rotor disk attitude and a secondary propeller. While this method has been effective for decades, it has made rotary-wing aircraft heavier and more complex. This single-motor drone cut the need for a secondary mechanism by constantly adjusting the speed of the motor — speeding it up produces more reaction torque while slowing it down applies opposite reaction torque. articles.title: Stratospheric airship flew from US to Japan to test sky cell tower concept
articles.summary:
Nearly 100 years after the dirigible Graf Zeppelin made the first nonstop airship journey across the Pacific Ocean, another airship has successfully completed a round-trip flight from New Mexico to Japan and back. But the significance of this modern feat was less about the journey’s length and more about its purpose: demonstrating how a lighter-than-air platform can act as a cell phone tower in the sky.
The trans-Pacific flight that took place over a month between August and September 2026 was the most notable milestone yet for Sceye, a US aerospace company based near Albuquerque, New Mexico. Sceye has developed an uncrewed platform filled with helium for buoyancy and equipped with an electric-powered propeller for active propulsion, allowing it to resist most strong winds and keep hovering over the same location for long periods. The platform also uses top-mounted solar panels and onboard batteries to stay powered for stratospheric operations around the clock.
“We can stay over an area of operation, and we do that in the stratosphere right around 60,000 feet, so we’re twice as high as air traffic and we’re above the jet stream, and yet 30 times closer than low-Earth orbit satellites,” Mikkel Frandsen, founder and CEO of Sceye, told Ars. “We can fly through day and night until the sun comes up the next morning and recharges the batteries, at which point we’re still at the same altitude and still over the same area of operation.”

The code runs with the same privileges as the Plex service.
The issues were reported to Plex on July 27, and the company confirmed them and awarded a bug bounty on August 4. On September 1, Plex announced it had already shipped fixes and asked server owners to upgrade.
A different researcher caught the attacks by setting up an internet-facing Plex honeypot running a vulnerable release. Before October 17, the decoy had drawn largely reconnaissance scans and generic attack attempts.
“As of this morning (Oct 17th), I finally saw in the wild exploitation,” the researcher wrote. The attackers used the publicly released exploit, the researcher said, though they may have tweaked the code.
The attackers were observed dropping a cryptocurrency miner built on XMRig. Later that day, a second program called myawesomeproxy also appeared on the honeypot. These scientists hope that fire-spotting satellites, AI tools and ancient land practices could preserve the world’s vulnerable permafrost—and the vast carbon it stores.
In the middle of an especially warm July in 2021, a wildfire ignited in a thick forest of black spruce and peeling paper birch trees on the northern campus of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks.
The blaze, possibly sparked by lightning, burned across the dry carpet of feather mosses and lichen before climbing into the crowns. By the time fire agencies responded, flames had reached 12 feet in length and sent up a 500-foot column of smoke.
A few days shy of the five-year anniversary of the Yankovich Road Fire, I followed three members of the Alaska Fire Science Consortium into the boreal forest, walking along cross-country ski trails lined by feathery field horsetail.
In 2024, the organization, which hosts presentations to keep wildfire managers abreast of new developments in fire science, helped turn the area into an educational walking trail, with interpretive signs posted along the route. About a half-mile in, the horizon opened up as we reached a sparse stand of naked, blackened tree trunks, stripped of needles and neighbors.
Hilary Shook, the coordinator of the consortium, stepped off the trail with her thaw probe, a T-shaped pointed metal rod used to detect the upper boundary of the permafrost, the ancient layer of frozen soil tha…

articles.title: Gemini 4 logra lo imposible y termina 'Minecraft' sin ayuda humana
articles.summary:
Google se ha apoyado en los videojuegos para demostrar lo que puede lograr su inteligencia artificial. Hace unos años, AlphaStar se convirtió en la primera IA en derrotar a un jugador profesional de StarCraft II, alcanzando el rango de Gran Maestro. Ahora toca el turno de Gemini 4, que consiguió vencer Minecraft sin intervención humana.
De acuerdo con una publicación científica de Google DeepMind, Gemini 4 Argon logró derrotar al Ender Dragon de Minecraft sin recibir ayuda durante una partida. Un equipo conformado por cuatro agentes de IA logró su objetivo y terminó el juego luego de casi 30 horas.
La prueba de DeepMind consistió en colocar a cuatro agentes de Gemini 4 Argon dentro de un mundo de supervivencia aleatorio en el que tenían el objetivo de acabar con el dragón. Los agentes no recibieron estrategias predefinidas ni herramientas especiales creadas para Minecraft. Cada uno controlaba a un jugador a través de Mineflayer y se coordinaba con los demás por el chat del juego y una memoria compartida.
El documento señala que los agentes se repartieron el trabajo desde el comienzo. En lugar de actuar como un sistema centralizado, la IA dividió el trabajo de forma espontánea, asignando tareas como recolectar recursos y alimentos, explorar el mapa o llevar a cabo tareas esenciales para avanzar. En el chat, los agentes se avisaban de amenazas, intercambiaban consejos de combate o se ayudaban mutuamente cuando uno perdía su equipo tras morir.

articles.title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more.
One such solution, called “dumbtv,” describes its mission on its GitHub page thus: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.”
Another, “cleanyourtv,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV.
While hacking consumer electronics devices to gain more control over their systems is hardly a new idea, the latest advances in AI technology have made such efforts much more accessible to anyone. With smart TVs in particular, the hacks come at a time when people have grown frustrated with being forced to watch ads and put up with their devices surveilling their viewing habits.
Modern smart TVs ship with a technology called automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what’s playing on the screen using screenshots, audio clips, or other forms of digital fingerprinting.

articles.title: DIY VR: How to build your own headset, and why you probably won't want to
articles.summary:
Virtual reality is in a bit of a weird place right now. After a lot of unfulfilled promise in the 1990s, it came back strong with the 2016 release of the Oculus Rift. For a while, it looked like VR, AR, XR, the metaverse, or whatever you wanted to call it, was going to be huge. Mark Zuckerberg was certainly convinced, and even Apple got in on the hype with its Vision Pro.
But by then momentum for alternate realities of every acronym was already in steady decline, and it only dwindled from there. The rate of development of new headsets has slowed, with many companies (including Apple) scaling back or shelving their efforts. While new releases like the Steam Frame and Pimax Dream Air are still happening, many of the most interesting developments in the space these days are on the enthusiast front.
That’s right, DIY VR is a thing, and with a couple hundred dollars in components, plus many hours of your time, you too can enter the immersive world of virtual reality while also experiencing the highs and lows of soldering, firmware flashing, and 3D printing. I rode that rollercoaster myself and learned why this is still a decidedly niche movement.

articles.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
articles.summary:
NestJS, the TypeScript framework for building server-side Node.js applications, has released version 12, a major release that moves its core packages to ESM, adds first-class Standard Schema validation, rebuilds the CLI and introduces an official observability SDK. It follows April's roadmap, and creator Kamil Myśliwiec's announcement on X has passed 1,100 likes and 66,000 views.
The ESM change is the headline, largely because it asks so little of existing teams. Core packages now ship as ESM, but CommonJS applications keep working through Node.js require(esm) support, which is why v12 requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. nest new now asks whether to generate a CJS or ESM project, with ESM projects defaulting to Vitest and oxlint, while Rspack replaces webpack as the monorepo bundler. Developer Anton Chapala's preview benchmarks found no meaningful startup or memory gains from ESM, concluding it "is a massive cleanup of tooling and configuration debt" rather than a performance upgrade.
Day-to-day ergonomics change most around validation. Route decorators such as @Body(), @Query() and @Param() accept a schema option taking any Standard Schema compatible object, so Zod, Valibot and ArkType work without third-party wrappers once the new pipe is registered.

In that world of startups, founders and investors, we learn to ask certain questions almost instinctively. How big can this become? How much capital will it take to get there? And, sooner or later, when do I get my money back, and at what multiple?
These are not cynical questions. They reflect the logic of venture capital, where investors put capital at risk expecting substantial returns and founders pursue growth, scale and eventually liquidity.
But there is a question we ask far less often: Are we building the companies we actually want to own, or the companies our funding models encourage us to build?
When success changes meaning
At an event recently, I found myself in a conversation with experienced tech entrepreneurs who had already built, scaled and exited companies.
One founder told the room that, knowing what she knows today, she would never have sold her first company. Another described how differently he is building his next venture after taking external capital and scaling rapidly the first time around.
These were successful entrepreneurs by conventional measures. Yet their experiences had changed how they thought about ownership, ambition and what they ultimately wanted from building a business. Nigeria has made progress in bringing more people into the formal financial system, but having a bank account does not necessarily mean being able to obtain a loan. While more Nigerians can now access financial services, borrowing costs, limited credit histories, and irregular incomes still shape who can obtain formal credit and on what terms.
According to the 2026 Access to Financial Services in Nigeria (A2F) survey by Enhancing Financial Innovation & Access (EFInA), formal financial inclusion rose to 73%, up from 64% in 2023. The proportion of adults excluded from the financial system fell from 26% to 21%. These figures show that financial inclusion is not the same as access to credit. Financial inclusion encompasses access to and use of services such as payments, savings, insurance and borrowing. A person may have a bank account, receive payments digitally and save through a formal institution without qualifying for a loan.

articles.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
Interesting research:
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. We study what changes when a solver improves with use. Our system pairs a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector with an open-weight VLM behind a confidence-based router, and runs entirely from screenshots and operating-system input events, with no browser automation or DOM access. It reaches 85.4% overall and 84.2% macro accuracy across 16 classes, exceeding either component alone. Every answer VLM produces also serves as a training label, so the detector absorbs categories it was never trained for, typically after one or two encounters and without human annotation. The same loop also repairs it. A CAPTCHA operator can perturb images against the publicly released detector and drive its accuracy to 0%, but the perturbations leave VLM untouched, and its labels let the detector recover. Under a year-long simulated arms race in which the CAPTCHA operator re-crafts its perturbations each month, the solver recovers every round, and a cheap ~70%-accurate open-weight teacher hardens it as effectively as a perfect oracle. “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration.

Brad Winderbaum, à la tête de Marvel Television, a remis les pendules à l’heure en octobre 2026 dans l’émission américaine The Brandon Davis Show. Selon lui, Daredevil Born Again n’a pas été arrêtée par la direction de Marvel pour cause de mauvaises audiences.
Selon lui, le plan a toujours été de découper cette nouvelle ère en trois actes bien distincts, à la manière des trade paperbacks (ces recueils de bandes dessinées que l’on aligne fièrement dans sa bibliothèque).
Une structure en 3 parties pour Daredevil
L’argumentaire de Winderbaum se veut poétique, mais il dissimule à peine une volonté d’imposer un cadre strict : la série originale Netflix comptait trois saisons, Daredevil Born Again aura exactement le même traitement. Une manière propre de fermer le chapitre sériel avant d’envisager la suite des événements pour l’avocat aveugle.
« Le plan a toujours été de s’arrêter à la saison 3. C’est comme deux coffrets de trois volumes sur une étagère : on boucle la série, puis on prend une grande respiration pour décider de la suite pour le personnage », résume Brad Winderbaum.
Pour cette ultime salve d’épisodes, les scénaristes n’ont pas cherché bien loin leur inspiration, piochant directement dans The Devil in Cell-Block D, l’arc qui ouvre en 2006 la période d’Ed Brubaker au scénario de Daredevil. At TechSparks 2026, technology leaders from ShareChat, Angel One, Amagi and Innovaccer said India’s next competitive edge will depend on deep industry expertise, customer insights, trust and the ability to turn AI into real-world solutions.
India’s technology industry has long relied on talent, cost efficiency and scale. But as artificial intelligence makes advanced tools more accessible, these advantages alone may no longer be enough to differentiate companies.
The next edge, according to technology leaders at TechSparks 2026, will come from how effectively companies use AI to solve specific problems, understand customers and build products that are difficult to replicate.
During a panel titled The New CTO Playbook: India’s Next Tech Advantage, Nitin Jain, CTO of ShareChat and Moj; Ajit Narayanan, CTO of Angel One; Srividhya Srinivasan, CTO of Amagi; and Ankit Maheshwari, founder and CTO of Innovaccer, discussed how Indian technology companies can remain competitive in an AI-driven market, at the 17th edition of YourStory’s flagship tech-startup event, TechSparks.
India’s complexity is an advantage
For ShareChat and Moj, India’s linguistic and cultural diversity offers an opportunity to build products for varied audiences. Nitin Jain said companies must account for differences in languages, devices, network quality and user preferences.

articles.title: Jubilee, FSD Africa partner with 7 BimaLab insurtechs to pilot inclusive insurance in Kenya - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
East African financial services group Jubilee and development agency FSD Africa have partnered with seven insurtech startups from the BimaLab Africa accelerator network to develop and pilot affordable insurance products for underserved Kenyans.
BimaLab, an FSD Africa initiative, has supported 135 startups across 28 African countries over the past six years, helping develop more than 300 insurance solutions that now reach over 6.5 million customers.
The programme targets SMEs, informal sector workers, farmers and low-income households, segments that remain largely uninsured. East Africa is estimated to have more than 10 million SMEs, which account for over 70 per cent of jobs, yet insurance penetration among the segment averages about one per cent.
The seven firms – Dukatech Solutions, Aura Insure Technologies, Inclusivity Solutions, DPE, Fiinovate, Agrails and Ibisa Network – were selected through a competitive process from BimaLab’s alumni network. They will go through an eight-week product co-creation process with Jubilee before joint pilots kick off in Kenya next month.
The work will focus on three areas – low-cost bundled and embedded insurance distribution, insurance solutions for SME ecosystems, and wellness and engagement models that link customers to health and care services. Successful solutions could later be rolled out in other East African markets.

articles.title: AI assistant startup Town nabs unicorn valuation 4 months after launch | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Town, a two-year-old, San Francisco-based startup developing AI assistants, nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B funding round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures. The company launched publicly just four months ago and said it reached millions of dollars in annual recurring revenue in a matter of weeks. It has raised at least $160 million to date, having previously announced a $55 million Series A round in June.
Town — founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze — is one of many AI assistants flooding the market right now. Town targets businesses, giving each employee an AI assistant called a Townie that helps with tasks by connecting to tools such as emails and calendars, as well as other core work systems. Employees’ Townies can talk to each other and share approved information; they can also now work with customers and others outside the company.
Alongside the funding, Town announced a shared workflow that automatically updates employees’ Townies with new business information rather than requiring each worker to update their own Townie. Andreessen Horowitz, Serena Ventures, and First Round Capital also participated in the round.
We’ve reached out to the company for comment.

articles.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
articles.summary:
Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
Millions of AI agents are descending on a web built for humans. Websites are trying to keep them out, but the arrival of these new visitors could transform the internet.
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.
Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people. Websites have long allowed bots to perform automated tasks, like capturing the content of web pages, but rules govern what they can access and how they behave. The web, after all, is designed primarily for people, even if we occasionally have to solve puzzles and captchas to prove we are not bots.
But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.
The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.

articles.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
articles.summary:
This week, Character.AI declared bankruptcy. While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry, court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand—potentially acquire most of Character.AI’s technology, and avoid the beleaguered startup’s many legal liabilities and obligations.
In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders.
The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing.
The move appears to be a new twist on what some have dubbed a “reverse acquihire,” a process in which a buyer carefully orchestrates a succession of deals with a target company, usually in an effort to hire key employees and obtain expansive license to use and build on the target company’s unique technology. Stripped of its employees, the target becomes a husk of itself.

articles.summary:
Home
                        TECHNICAL PAPERS
		
								October 19th, 2026 - 
								By: Technical Paper Link
								
							
Researchers at Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign published a technical paper titled “Agentic AI for Heterogeneous System Design Across Chip, Scale-Up, and Scale-Out Domains.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“The design space of modern AI/HPC systems has expanded rapidly across compute architectures, including GPUs, dataflow processors, and RISC-V accelerators; memory technologies, including HBM, GDDR, and SRAM; and interconnects such as NVLink, UALink, Infinity Fabric, InfiniBand, Slingshot, and Ultra Ethernet. No single architecture is optimal across LLM training, LLM serving, and AI-coupled HPC workloads, while the resulting combinatorial design space is too large for manual exploration. We present ArchAgent, a hierarchical multi- agent framework in which an LLM-based planner decomposes system design into chip, scale-up, and scale-out subproblems, each handled by specialist agents.”

articles.summary:
Un número de teléfono puede parecer un dato menor, pero suele estar vinculado a cuentas bancarias, correos electrónicos, redes sociales y aplicaciones de mensajería. En Centroamérica, conocer los riesgos asociados a su exposición permite a los usuarios detectar maniobras de fraude antes de que los delincuentes obtengan información, dinero o acceso a servicios digitales.
La firma de ciberseguridad ESET Latinoamérica advirtió recientemente que un número telefónico puede convertirse en el punto de partida para fraudes, robos de cuentas y suplantaciones de identidad. El dato, por sí solo, no permite ingresar de forma directa a un celular, leer conversaciones de WhatsApp ni acceder a una cuenta bancaria. El riesgo aparece cuando los atacantes lo combinan con información disponible en internet o con engaños dirigidos a la víctima.
Para los usuarios de países centroamericanos, donde los teléfonos son una herramienta habitual para recibir transferencias, coordinar entregas, comunicarse con familiares en el exterior y validar operaciones digitales, la advertencia plantea medidas concretas de prevención.

The company now wants to understand what happened, and how a cargo of such valuable consumer electronics can disappear inside an international airport without leaving any trace. articles.title: Cheaper fibre fees don't spark Nigerian infrastructure investment
articles.summary:
Nigeria’s states take widely different approaches to the cost of laying fibre-optic cables. Some have waived Right of Way (RoW) fees; others charge the ₦145-per-metre benchmark, while Ogun State charges up to ₦6,600 ($4.84) per metre. Yet these differences do not neatly explain where fibre infrastructure has been built, raising questions about what else drives investment.
Administrative reforms and project-specific concessions may help offset high fees, but there is little evidence that they do so systematically. The Lagos State Infrastructure Maintenance and Regulatory Agency (LASIMRA) describes itself as a one-stop regulator for utility infrastructure, and the state has announced an online permitting system to streamline approvals for fibre, masts and towers. However, the announcement does not establish whether the system has reduced processing times or costs or removed requirements such as environmental approvals.
Ogun has also reportedly waived RoW charges for a specific 250-kilometre MainOne deployment, but that historical concession does not establish that similar incentives are generally available today. There is no verified evidence of a telecom-specific tax-break programme that explains the substantial fibre networks in these high-fee states. Without access to operators’ permits, concession agreements and investment decisions, it remains unclear whether incentives offset the charges or whether companies invest despite them.

Based on Gemma 4 and released under the Apache 2.0 license, Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 is a compact, open-weight, multimodal embedding model designed to make semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) more efficient while optimizing performance for on-device deployment.
Designed to run on consumer hardware such as mobile devices and laptops, EmbeddingGemma 2 delivers low-latency semantic representations for on-device applications, like search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), classification, and clustering.
Thanks to its multimodal capabilities, EmbeddingGemma 2 supports a wide range of retrieval tasks, including finding relevant documents, screenshots, and recordings in response to a query, searching source code using natural language, and retrieving video content based on textual descriptions.
EmbeddingGemma 2's key feature, Google says, is its ability to represent text, code, images, video, and audio in a unified 768-dimensional embedding space. This enables developers to build retrieval systems that search across different media types without maintaining separate, incompatible embedding spaces for different media types.
Despite coming from different modalities, the embeddings generated by EmbeddingGemma 2 occupy the same dimensional space and can be compared on their semantic similarity.

Siemens Software Center handles the download, installation, activation and updating of software that customers have bought, and it can also be used to start free trials.

Siemens disclosed the flaw on October 15 in an advisory that assigned it a CVSS v4 score of 8.4. Two days later, the company updated the advisory to tell customers that version 4.0.9.8 resolves the issue.

articles.title: Precision Timing Special Report - EE Times
articles.summary:
Every electronic system depends on accurate timing. Crystals and oscillators supply the reference signals that keep processors synchronized, communications stable, and data moving reliably, and nearly every other function on a board is measured against them. A timing device is also among the smallest and least expensive parts in a design, which is why it is often specified late and compared on little more than frequency and price.
That shortcut has become harder to justify. Data rates have climbed, so reference jitter now shows up directly in link margin. Products are deployed where conditions are uncontrolled: on machinery, in vehicles, on utility infrastructure, and inside sealed enclosures. More systems run on batteries for years between service visits, which puts a premium on nanoampere timekeeping. Emissions requirements, safety expectations, and long production lifecycles all push the timing decision earlier in the schedule.
The range of options has widened at the same time. Quartz crystals, packaged clock oscillators, temperature-compensated oscillators, real-time clock modules, MEMS devices, and atomic references each solve a different problem, and several of them look similar in a parametric search. The useful comparison is rarely between technologies in the abstract. It is between a specific device and the requirements of a specific design.

El director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, confirmó que la empresa va a construir un robot humanoide y adelantó que habrá una demostración pública en 2027, aunque descartó que esos robots circulen por la calle en el corto plazo.
La confirmación llegó en dos entrevistas distintas. En el pódcast Sources, le preguntaron de manera directa si OpenAI fabricaría un robot humanoide. Su respuesta fue breve: “We will” (lo vamos a hacer), según citó Engadget.
A Fortune, Altman agregó el horizonte de tiempo: “Creo que vamos a tener una demostración genial en 2027... no creo que vaya a haber robots caminando por las calles por varios años más”, dijo, de acuerdo con el mismo reporte de Engadget, replicado también por el medio indio Mint.
OpenAI no precisó qué va a mostrar esa demostración, qué forma tendrá el robot ni cuándo alguien ajeno a la empresa podrá acercarse a uno. articles.title: The Future of Web Apps: Will AI Agents Generate UIs on the Fly?
articles.summary:
Rachel Lee Nabors, former React core team member, dives into the architecture and philosophy behind local-first applications, exploring how small language models (SLMs) running directly on-device can deliver privacy-focused, low-latency, and cost-effective alternatives to cloud-hosted LLM wrappers. Rachel shares key insights on evaluating models with golden datasets and leveraging client-side AI for moderation and social content aggregation.
The discussion also looks ahead to the future of web and application architectures in an AI-driven ecosystem. From the potential rise of OS-level personal agents and dynamic UI rendering standards like A2UI, to the evolving skill set required of software engineers.
Key Takeaways
- Building apps local-first delivers fast, offline capability for users while keeping cloud infrastructure costs low for developers.
- Utilizing SLMs locally (like Llama 3.2B) avoids high API costs, reduces latency, and protects PII compared to large cloud LLMs.
- Systematic evaluation using golden datasets is essential for right-sizing models and picking the best option for specific tasks like summarization or moderation.
- OS-level personal agents and standardized UI schemas (like A2UI) may replace traditional web apps and native interfaces for consumption.
- Software engineering is moving beyond basic code generation towards computer science fundamentals, system design, and AI collaboration.

The Japanese giant says subsets of the data contained personally identifiable information and other sensitive details, but most records contained no identifying info.

Nikkei Inc. is a major Japanese business news and financial information group, owner of Financial Times, the country’s largest business-focused media company.

Nikkei revoked the abused credentials and notified the Personal Information Protection Commission on October 11.

Now, though, AI coding tools are making that cloning process so efficient that many developers are getting extremely cautious about sharing their early work too widely.
Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend, delaying the launch of a planned public demo for its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflux, which had been set to go live with today’s launch of Steam Next Fest.
In a post on social media Friday evening, the Alliance Arts team wrote that, in addition to concerns about managing streaming restrictions, “we’re concerned that the demo’s content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game’s presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools and that such works could be released before our launch.”

articles.title: This mod lets Nvidia GeForce owners run a custom VBIOS without flashing the card

Enthusiast zone: Nvidia's signed firmware has kept BIOS modding off the table for GeForce owners for the most part. A new set of tools sidesteps that lock rather than breaking it, loading a custom VBIOS through the driver itself. It reopens a door enthusiasts thought was closed, but it arrives on a platform where power connectors are already at risk of melting on high-end GPUs and a single driver update could shut it down. Proceed carefully.
A developer has released three tools that let GeForce RTX 30, 40 and 50 series owners run a modified VBIOS without writing to the card's flash chip: a VBIOS editor for Windows and Linux, plus separate loaders for each operating system.
The cool trick is that nothing gets flashed. On Windows, the loader stores the edited image in the GPU's driver registry key, a spot where Nvidia's driver already checks for a VBIOS override every time the device starts. The tool then restarts the GPU, and the driver's GSP firmware boots from the custom image instead of the one on the card.
The Linux version takes a different route, patching Nvidia's open kernel modules so the GSP firmware starts with the custom image. Both projects build on earlier override research, which the developer credits directly.

Son code est publié en open source sur le dépôt GitHub ovh/ovhcloud-cli. Il s’adresse surtout aux développeurs et aux administrateurs système, dont les machines contiennent justement beaucoup d’accès sensibles.

articles.title: You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
articles.summary:
You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
Less flashing means less worrying, but a modified VBIOS may still brick a GPU in other ways.
Panchovix on GitHub recently released a VBIOS configurator for RTX 30-to 50-series cards that doesn’t require flashing. The loader provides a UI for easy configuration and lowers the risk of bricking your GPU by avoiding a risky flash process, and it's available for Linux, too.
Software like MSI Afterburner or ASUS GPU Tweak is often the go-to tool for quickly changing your graphics card’s settings; however, those tools have hard limits to how much you can push the graphics card. If you want to tweak your GPU beyond the firmware’s set limits, you can change it by tweaking the parameters in the VBIOS. Configuring VBIOS is similar to changing BIOS settings in the BOOT menu. With the VBIOS loader, you can change settings beyond the firmware’s hard limits.
The way it works is by storing the modified VBIOS image in the GPU’s register key; as the Nvidia driver looks for a VBIOS override on startup, it finds the VBIOS image and restarts, applying the override settings. The flash chip on the graphics card is not overwritten, reducing the risk of bricking your GPU. However, this does not protect the card from any extreme settings that could destroy electrical components; it merely provides a safer and more convenient way to adjust and apply VBIO…

articles.title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
articles.summary:
Open source Windows alternative ReactOS has reached a major milestone: The operating system can now be installed directly onto an NT Files System drive partition. As reported by Phoronix, the move to NTFS clears a long-standing hurdle for the project and brings it one step closer to finally reaching beta.
Prior to this latest announcement, ReactOS required users to keep a FAT32 partition for installations. A proprietary Microsoft-developed filesystem, NTFS can trace its roots back through the Windows NT family lineage starting in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1. The variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001 remains the standard used by most Windows systems today. With ReactOS’s stated goal of reaching binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, being confined to FAT32 partitions was a practical barrier to clear on the way to reproducing the Windows environment.
However, users looking to hop off the Windows train shouldn’t be grabbing their bags just yet. ReactOS wrote that the new driver still “lacks caching (which causes inferior performance), journaling and security support.” So while the new driver is here, even the most intrepid of OS tinkerers should tread carefully. The ReactOS team warned in its announcement on X that there are still “potentially undiscovered bugs.”

Ripple effect: One of the most popular pieces of computer software is about to deliver a better experience on Linux machines. The Steam client is going 64-bit, providing feature parity with versions designed to run on different operating systems.
A recent Steam Client Beta update brought the program into the 64-bit era on Linux. The native Linux version of the massively popular gaming client is now a 64-bit application, which means it gains access to a few significant enhancements and, hopefully, a more reliable software experience.
Until last week's beta update, Steam's main binary ran as a 32-bit application even on 64-bit Linux distros. Some components, such as steamwebhelper, were already 64-bit. Now the main client uses 64-bit code as well, which should significantly expand memory access and improve the software's overall security.
Steam is going 64-bit, but Linux users will still need to provide 32-bit libraries and graphics drivers for compatibility reasons. Valve said Linux operating systems that only work with 64-bit software are not supported just yet, which might further complicate the job of distro maintainers. The Fedora team floated dropping 32-bit library support last year, but withdrew the proposal after pushback over Steam compatibility – or lack thereof.
